Source: Source: Discussion #96 (answered 2026-09-07): significant actions are those that "materially affect the event or its arrangements, such as submission, approval/rejection, coordinator assignment/reassignment, important event information changes, venue booking decisions, equipment reservation changes, confirmation, rescheduling or cancellation." A complete audit-history function is not required for Release 1.
Estimate rationale: Estimate: 3. Normal story. Only two places write entries: coordinator assignment (SPM-30) and saving event information (SPM-62), and SPM-62 already works out which important changes a save made. What makes it a 3 rather than a 2: - A schema change. The status history holds only a from-status and a to-status, so an entry that is not a status change (a reassignment, an information change on a Planning event) has nowhere to go. It needs a new table or a wider one, with a migration; that is a shared table, so it goes through the team chat first. - Before and after values for date and time and expected attendance, and one entry for a save that makes several changes. - The History tab from SPM-95 has to show two kinds of entry in one date order. SPM-97 reuses whatever is decided here for storing entries, so this should be built before it.

Title: Record Venue Booking and Equipment Changes in Event History
Source: Source: Discussion #96 (answered 2026-09-07): significant actions are those that "materially affect the event or its arrangements, such as submission, approval/rejection, coordinator assignment/reassignment, important event information changes, venue booking decisions, equipment reservation changes, confirmation, rescheduling or cancellation." A complete audit-history function is not required for Release 1.
Estimate rationale: Estimate: 5. About the same as Request Venue Booking (SPM-42, our 5 reference). Each entry is simple to write, and it assumes the place to store entries comes from SPM-96, so there is no schema change of its own. What makes it a 5 rather than a 3 is breadth and testing: - Six kinds of action across three owners' areas: booking requested and booking decided (venues), equipment outcome recorded and reviewed equipment line changed or removed (equipment), arrangement marked not required or required again (SPM-33), and arrangements flagged for review by a venue change (SPM-39) or an information change (SPM-62). - Each entry has to be written in the same transaction as the action, so a refused or failed action leaves none, and each needs its own test for that. - One rule is not a plain "always write": an equipment line that has not been reviewed writes no entry, a reviewed or reserved one does. If planning poker puts it at 8, split it in two: venue booking entries, and equipment and arrangement entries. If SPM-96 is not built first, add its schema work to this one.
